newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares languish at noon on poor demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares languish at noon on poor demand.

text.p: Singapore shares languished at midday on Monday, dampened by poor institutional and retail demand ahead of April trade figures here and expectations of a rise in U.S. interest rates, dealers aid.
They said funds also continued to liquidate exposure to Southeast Asia, after volatility in the Thai baht last week.
The bulk of activity focused on debutant Tye Soon, which saw 27.57 million shares traded. They ended the morning at Singapore $0.47 cents against an IPO price of S$0.31,

The Straits Times Industrials Index was down 12.77 points at 2,047.73, with decliners outpacing gainers at 200 against 48. "The market is in a consolidation. Next direction will be set after April non-oil exports," one dealer said.
Economists, polled by Reuters ahead of the release of the data on Tuesday, projected a year-on-year rise of 0.5 percent in April.
Malaysia'a MBF Capital was active, up five cents to S$2.49, fuelled by rumours of a merger with Suria Capital.
